scenarios.answer: println adds a newline after the text and print does not.

println.rule: println(String x) behaves as though it calls print(x) and then println(); println() terminates the current line by writing the line separator string.
println.student_evidence: println adds a newline after the text

print.rule: print(String s) prints the string (or "null" for a null reference); print(int) etc. print the value's string form; no line terminator is written.

edges.logic: print leaves the cursor on the same line after printing; println moves the cursor to the next line after printing.
edges.student_evidence: println adds a newline after the text and print does not

scenarios.answer: So first Java looks at the code and the first thing it does is print A, which always happens no matter what x is, and then it checks whether x is even, and 17 is not even because 17 divided by 2 leaves 1, so it skips the whole first part with B, C and D, and goes to the else part, where it checks 17 % 5, which is 2, so it prints E, and then after that inner if-else it prints G, so overall I think the answer would be AEG, which makes sense because…
